observations.statement: Usage is defined as a projection over the canonical seglog, with redb rollups serving 5h/7d and dashboard values; usage.jsonl is limited to mirror or migration-input status rather than canonical rollup truth.
Canonical navigation is object-first, and the attempt, provider-attempt, Usage, and receipt bridges have distinct lineage roles.
Record, bundle, and view exports are explicitly distinct authority classes.

The per-thread context circle is a split inspect/action affordance: hover presents status, click reveals Compact Now, More Details opens the Context Detail Pane, and app-wide Usage remains the aggregate view.
Quota and pressure projections may consume mixed-quality signals, but incomplete live-API availability must be disclosed rather than rendered as exact quota truth.
Cursor quota presentation prohibits invented remaining-request balances and requires source disclosure for provider, team-admin, runtime-inferred, and editor-refusal evidence.
Codex ChatGPT-plan and API-key usage are separate entitlement buckets that cannot share one pressure or cooldown pool, and their UI labels and evidence meanings are differentiated.

Copilot premium exhaustion, billing policy, organization policy, entitlement absence, and billing-entity setup are distinct states, with hard-block claims requiring explicit entitlement, policy, or runtime-refusal evidence.
Gemini Direct is a key-only direct provider, active Google CLI-runtime evidence belongs to Antigravity, and unknown quota values require source-qualified wording.

candidate_findings.title: Blocked-owner eight-kind taxonomy and escalation ladder are not enumerated
candidate_findings.problem: The owner-section heading promises an eight-kind blocked-owner taxonomy and escalation-ladder surfaces, but this core window does not name the eight kinds, define their owner values, or state escalation transitions; related clauses only require preservation of ownership, severity, follow-through, and blocked rows.
candidate_findings.consequence: Provider-specific blocked reasons and cross-surface blocked or approval-wait rows cannot be mapped to one deterministic owner and escalation model from this window.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The exact eight-kind enum, reason-to-kind mapping, owner authority, escalation levels, transition triggers, persistence rules, and resolution behavior are absent.

candidate_findings.title: Projection trust states are not connected to an exact action-gating matrix
candidate_findings.problem: The window names projection trust and action gating, accepts mixed signal sources, and exposes confidence, settlement, freshness, and redaction concepts, but it does not define which actions are enabled, disabled, advisory-only, or blocked for each trust/value state.
candidate_findings.consequence: The same inferred, stale, unsettled, or redacted value can drive materially different controls and warnings across implementations.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: A canonical trust-state vocabulary and a state-by-action gating table, including precedence among source class, confidence, settlement, freshness, redaction, and explicit refusal evidence, are not stated.

candidate_findings.title: Analytics scan source precedence is ambiguous
candidate_findings.problem: The scan language permits aggregation over the seglog and a JSONL mirror, or over a JSONL mirror alone, while also prohibiting ad hoc usage.jsonl scans as canonical rollup production. The allowed mirror fallback boundary is not exact.
candidate_findings.consequence: Rollup values and their trust status can vary depending on whether an implementation selects seglog, a mirror, or both when the sources differ in checkpoint or completeness.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Deterministic source precedence, mirror eligibility, checkpoint and freshness requirements, mismatch handling, and fallback failure behavior are not defined.

candidate_findings.title: Refresh and freshness behavior lacks an operational state contract
candidate_findings.problem: The UI must mark stale values and expose Last updated and Refresh, while background refresh is described only by examples such as periodic or after runs. No freshness threshold, cadence, trigger precedence, concurrent-refresh behavior, or refresh-failure state is specified.
candidate_findings.consequence: Identical values can be presented as current or stale at different times, and the explicit Refresh action can have inconsistent observable outcomes.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Per-source freshness budgets, timestamp meaning, background trigger rules, in-flight and failure states, retry or backoff semantics, and the transition back to current are absent.

candidate_findings.title: Always-visible placement leaves consequential surface selection unresolved
candidate_findings.problem: The placement rule allows any one of dashboard, header, or a dedicated Usage page, while the adjacent rule requires 5h/7d limits to be always visible. The window does not state which surface is mandatory or how a dedicated page alone satisfies always-visible behavior.
candidate_findings.consequence: Builders can produce incompatible navigation and visibility behavior while each selecting one permitted placement.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The mandatory host surface or surfaces, per-platform visibility rules, compact versus expanded content, and behavior when no current quota value exists are unspecified.

candidate_findings.title: Alert thresholds do not define a deterministic lifecycle
candidate_findings.problem: Approaching-limit warnings are optional and use 80 percent only as an example, while thresholds are described as configurable and quiet suppression applies only to advisory resurfacing. The window does not define default enablement, comparison boundaries, hysteresis, deduplication, rearming, or when a threshold warning becomes a canonical blocked state.
candidate_findings.consequence: The same usage sequence can produce missed, repeated, or differently classified alerts across surfaces.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Canonical threshold defaults, configuration scope, crossing semantics, repeat and reset rules, advisory-versus-blocked classification, and interaction with quiet windows are absent.

candidate_findings.title: Event-ledger identity requirements are not reconciled with attempt-centric routing
candidate_findings.problem: Storage and routing clauses require project, run, package, lane, attempt, UsageRecord, and runtime-object identity, but the event-ledger section lists tier and session fields and filters only as examples. It does not state the minimum canonical identity carried by each row or filter.
candidate_findings.consequence: Ledger rows may omit the identities required for canonical subject opening, attribution, or project/run/package/lane scoping.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The required event-row identity fields, required columns and filters, route-target derivation, and mapping of legacy tier/session fields into attempt-centric identity are not specified.

candidate_findings.title: Event-ledger export is not mapped to the record, bundle, or view taxonomy
candidate_findings.problem: The document sharply distinguishes record, bundle, and view export authority, but the event-ledger requirement says only to retain export such as JSON. It does not classify that action or define whether filters and selections alter the authority of the output.
candidate_findings.consequence: A JSON action can emit either exact canonical records or a filtered presentation summary without a deterministic contract for identity, refs, manifest, or authority labeling.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The event-ledger export class, default class, filter and selection semantics, output envelope, manifest requirement, and user-visible authority label are not stated.

candidate_findings.title: Retention is a placeholder rather than an executable lifecycle policy
candidate_findings.problem: The retention section calls for a policy and gives storage technologies as examples, while cleanup depends on there being no retention reason. It does not define any duration, scope, deletion unit, compaction behavior, exception, or retention-reason vocabulary.
candidate_findings.consequence: Disk bounding and preservation of 5h/7d or historical views cannot be applied deterministically, and cleanup eligibility cannot be evaluated from this window.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Retention periods by record class and scope, purge or compaction boundaries, protected-history exceptions, retention-reason values, and cleanup interaction are absent.

candidate_findings.title: Mid-stream usage states lack exact names and transitions
candidate_findings.problem: Mid-stream totals must use explicit in-progress states, and UsageRecord presentation refers to value-state, settlement, freshness, and authority concepts, but the window does not enumerate the state values or define transitions for start, partial update, finalization, cancellation, failure, or correction.
candidate_findings.consequence: Provisional and final totals can be persisted, labeled, and reconciled differently across chat, Usage, and debug surfaces.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The usage-value state enum, transition triggers, finalization authority, correction behavior, and interaction among in-progress, settlement, freshness, and estimated-cost states are not specified.

candidate_findings.title: Cursor canonical source-class tokens lack normalization rules
candidate_findings.problem: The canonical list includes `inferred_from_runtime_refusal`, `inferred-from-runtime/editor-refusal`, and `/editor-refusal`, while the disclosure rule uses broader runtime-inferred and editor-refusal wording. The window does not say whether these are distinct stored values, aliases, or hierarchical categories.
candidate_findings.consequence: Producers, persisted records, filters, and UI labels can use incompatible identifiers for the same refusal evidence.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: One canonical source-class enum, alias and migration mapping, distinction criteria, and display-label mapping are absent.

candidate_findings.title: Optional analytics has no exact delivery boundary
candidate_findings.problem: The executive summary calls analytics optional, the analytics section says support it over time and allows multiple placements, while analytics scan jobs are foundational to rollup production. The window does not distinguish required analytics infrastructure from required or deferred analytics UI capabilities.
candidate_findings.consequence: Feature scope and completion can differ materially between an implementation with rollups only and one with analytics views, dimensions, cost breakdowns, and reporting.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: The must-have versus deferred capability set, milestone boundary, required aggregation dimensions, required cost views, and acceptance boundary for analytics are unspecified.

candidate_findings.title: Usage-specific acceptance evidence is unspecified
candidate_findings.problem: The window identifies deterministic verification and evidence contracts for the storage stack, but it does not name acceptance evidence for Usage-specific behaviors such as stale marking, refresh, hover and click branching, compaction dispatch, detail focusing, source qualification, or final-value transitions.
candidate_findings.consequence: Conformance of the stated Usage interactions cannot be determined from the evidence obligations present in this window.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Required fixtures, interaction cases, runtime receipts, expected state transitions, and evidence records for the Usage UI and command behavior are absent.

candidate_findings.title: Account-switch and pressure-history event contracts are named but not structurally defined
candidate_findings.problem: The document requires actor-scoped snapshots, first-class `account_switch_event` and `account_pressure_episode` records, shared consumers, account and execution identity fields, and bridge precedence, but it does not define either event's required envelope or transition semantics.
candidate_findings.consequence: Usage, History, Ledger, Orchestrator, Dashboard, and Account/Usage Pressure projections can construct different durable histories from the same switch or pressure episode.
candidate_findings.missing_or_ambiguous_obligation: Required event fields, canonical identifiers, timestamps, actor and account before/after values, reason and evidence fields, episode opening and closing rules, deduplication, ordering, and idempotency are absent.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Canonical storage authority is explicit: seglog owns the append-only event source, redb owns rollups and projections, and usage.jsonl is not canonical rollup truth.

Deep-link and bridge authority is explicit: navigation is object-first, attempt_id is the local anchor, provider_attempt_ref is the provider trace handle, usage_event_ref is the Usage bridge, and receipts remain external side-effect lineage.
The semantic distinction among record export, bundle export, and view export is explicit even though the event-ledger action is not assigned to one of them.

The non-binding OpenCode behavior does not control the canonical chat interaction; the canonical rules explicitly define the context circle, hover module, Compact Now branch, More Details branch, and app-wide Usage boundary.

Per-thread cost authority is explicit: canonical UsageRecord projections are primary, normalization is limited to marked estimates or non-authoritative values, and provider counting semantics gate token-component display.
Cursor presentation explicitly forbids treating inferred per-run evidence as an exact remaining-request balance and requires evidence-source disclosure.
Codex plan-backed and API-billed buckets are explicitly separate, and login-status evidence is explicitly excluded from usage-quantity or quota evidence.
Copilot blocked causes are explicitly differentiated, and hard-block semantics require entitlement, policy, or runtime-refusal evidence rather than metrics alone.
Gemini Direct is explicitly key-only and source-qualified unknown quota wording is required; Gemini CLI is explicitly retired lineage rather than an active provider row.
Quiet suppression is explicitly limited to advisory resurfacing and cannot remove canonical blocked or approval-wait rows.

unknowns.statement: The exact argument, result, and error schemas for the canonical compaction command, shared route-target payload, and Context Detail data contract may be defined in referenced contract documents.
unknowns.why_unresolved_within_capsule: Those referenced documents are outside the allowed capsule, and this window provides names and behavior but not their full schemas.

unknowns.statement: The referenced storage contract may define analytics source precedence, checkpoint consistency, failure behavior, and the complete UsageRecord schema.
unknowns.why_unresolved_within_capsule: The window delegates storage and Context Detail dependencies to storage-plan but does not include that contract's contents.

unknowns.statement: A per-platform matrix for plan-detection sources and live versus after-run refresh capability may exist in the referenced AGENTS or newfeatures material.
unknowns.why_unresolved_within_capsule: This window requires that support be documented and points to those sources, but the matrix itself is not present in the allowed excerpt.

unknowns.statement: Provider-owned documents may further specify exact quota windows, reset semantics, or refusal payloads for Cursor, Copilot, Claude Code, and Gemini.
unknowns.why_unresolved_within_capsule: This window states source-qualified provider behavior but the referenced provider contracts and external APIs are outside the capsule and external research is forbidden.

exact_evidence_refs.exact_quote: ### Projection trust and action gating
### Blocked-owner eight-kind taxonomy and escalation ladder surfaces

5h/7d and dashboard numbers are served from **redb rollups** produced by **analytics scan jobs** that aggregate over the seglog (and any JSONL mirror); the Usage view reads these rollups rather than scanning the ledger on demand.
| **Analytics scan jobs** | Scan seglog (or JSONL mirror) for counters; compute tool latency distributions, error rates, usage-by-window; persist rollups in redb for fast dashboard/Usage queries. |

Until this stack exists, any temporary compatibility path MUST still preserve the canonical pipeline: 5h/7d and dashboard windows are owned by rollups, not by ad hoc `usage.jsonl` scans. `usage.jsonl` may still appear as a human-readable mirror or Ledger compatibility input during migration, but it is not the canonical rollup source.

seglog owns the append-only event source, redb owns durable KV `/settings/state`, checkpoints, projections, and rollups, Tantivy owns search indices, and any JSONL or `usage.jsonl` output is a projector mirror rather than canonical truth.

Usage `/runtime/storage` paths and artifacts are scoped per-project, per-run, per-package, and per-lane; old tier/workspace-only layouts remain migration inputs and must not replace canonical project/run/package/lane identity.

Settings and help surfaces such as `/help/project-status`, `/event/alert`, blocked-sequence, startup-recovery, and DAE policy outcomes must preserve ownership, severity, persistence, and follow-through rather than becoming loose usage warnings.

GUI deep-links no longer use `run_id/thread_id/timestamp`, `/thread_id/timestamp`, `usage_event_seq`, broad timestamp filters, or tier-based `usage.jsonl` rollups as canonical navigation. They resolve object-first pivots through `usage_event_ref`, UsageRecord identity, runtime object identity, and Ledger/Usage route targets.

Usage and storage are attempt-centric for runtime attribution and preserve tier-centric labels only as compatibility vocabulary. Durable switch and pressure history uses actor-scoped snapshots plus first-class account-switch and pressure-episode records instead of only per-attempt `recent_switch_reason` or `account_switch_reason` fields.

Usage export semantics stay distinct: record export returns exact `/records` with stable ids, canonical ids, `/refs`, metadata, and schema-aware payloads; bundle export packages records, Evidence items, attached `/blobs/files`, thread export/share payloads, selected-object bundles, `.pm-bundle` configuration manifests, JSONL/JSON run-history artifacts, and a manifest; view export produces user-facing filtered table/list/chart output, CSV/JSON summaries, search results, analytics views, and graph `/render` convenience output without becoming canonical record truth.

`runtime-story` and audit surfaces consume append-only `account_switch_event` and `account_pressure_episode` history so Usage, History, Ledger, Orchestrator, Dashboard, and Account/Usage Pressure projections share the same durable facts; switch-history is an owned event family, not an under-owned view-only hint.

Shared runtime identity and bridged-provider envelopes expose `requested_account_id?`, `effective_account_id?`, execution-scope fields, `actor_kind`, and `execution_role` so Usage can attribute account and actor context without duplicating provider ownership.

Bridge-field precedence is explicit: `attempt_id` stays the local runtime anchor; `provider_attempt_ref?` appears on the `attempt_record` as the provider/runtime execution trace handle; `usage_event_ref` is the Usage bridge; and receipt refs remain external side-effect lineage.

Quota and pressure detection accept mixed signal sources: runtime outcomes, provider capabilities, heuristic `/log-derived` hints, and explicit `/pressure` evidence. Usage labels incomplete live-API availability rather than presenting inferred pressure as exact provider quota truth.

Quiet suppression only affects advisory resurfacing. Attention center and project badges must preserve canonical blocked and `/approval-wait` rows with precise owner and reason metadata, even when a quiet window is active.
Usage freshness is a user-trust requirement: stale values must be visibly marked with `Last updated` and an explicit `Refresh` action so old numbers are never presented as current.

Usage consumes `/package` and `/worktree` cleanup state only after owner records mark stale lanes or worktrees `cleanup_eligible`: lane/package completion, graph-patch supersession, revoked/reopened flow via `/reopened`, and completed recovery may make old backing removable only when no retention reason remains.

`cmd.nav.open_usage_subject` resolves canonical Usage/Ledger identity from `usage_event_ref` or an equivalent usage target; domain-specific usage commands are wrappers over the shared route/subject model, not independent argument families.

`/multi-account` usage surfaces keep configurable thresholds, platform quota visibility, rate-limit/reset countdowns, project-scoped usage storage, dashboard widgets, runtime event persistence, and usage + ledger + analytics rollups in one Usage projection model.
otherwise Usage follows this document's normalized UsageRecord/value-state contracts and `Plans/FinalGUISpec.md` presentation constraints.
Goals: show 5h/7d usage and plan type where available, surface event-level usage (ledger) and optional analytics, and warn when approaching limits so users can switch platform or pause.

| **Plans/Progression_Gates.md + Plans/evidence.schema.json** | Validation contract for the storage stack (seglog + redb + Tantivy + projectors + analytics scan) through deterministic verifier gates and evidence requirements. |
- **5h and 7d windows:** Show current usage vs limit (e.g. "5h: X / Y", "7d: X / Y") per platform where the platform or org API provides it.

- **Placement:** Always visible in at least one of: dashboard, header, or a dedicated **Usage** page. Tier config / setup should show current usage when selecting a platform so users can avoid platforms near limit.
- **Refresh:** Background refresh (e.g. periodic or after runs) so numbers stay up to date without blocking the UI. Document which platforms support "live" vs "after-run" stats.
- **Always-visible limits:** Match UX expectations set by tools like [yume](https://aofp.github.io/yume/) -- 5h and 7d usage always visible so users don't need a manual "usage" command.
- **Approaching limit:** Optional warning when usage is near limit (e.g. 80% of 5h window) so the user can switch tier or pause.
- **Rate limit hit:** When a run hits quota/rate limit, surface a clear message and, where possible, suggested action (e.g. "Try again after X" or "Switch platform"); link to the Usage view.

- **Event-level log:** Keep the existing concept of an event ledger (platform, operation, tokens in/out, cost, tier/session) so users can inspect per-request usage. This may remain the current "Ledger" page or be presented as a tab/section under a unified **Usage** area.
- **Filtering and export:** Retain filtering (e.g. by type, tier, session) and export (e.g. JSON) as part of the Usage feature.
- **Aggregated view:** Over time, support an analytics view that aggregates usage by time window, platform, project, or tier (as in newfeatures §7). Can be a separate page or a section under Usage.

- **Cost tracking and attribution:** Where data is available (from platform APIs), show cost breakdowns by model, project, and date (see [openclaudecto](https://github.com/josharsh/openclaudecto), [yume analytics](https://aofp.github.io/yume/)).
- **Retention:** Policy for how long to keep usage/ledger data (e.g. file-based or redb-backed) to bound disk use while supporting 5h/7d and historical views.
OpenCode Desktop implementation reference (non-binding):
Per-thread context/usage in chat is a split inspect/action affordance rather than a direct jump to a chat-shell usage panel.

- the chat header context circle is always the entrypoint for per-thread context state
- hover opens a lightweight status module showing `Usage`, `Tokens`, estimated `Cost`, and `More Details`
- click reveals the `Compact Now` action instead of immediately opening the detail surface
- selecting `Compact Now` dispatches the canonical compaction command for that thread
- selecting `More Details` opens or focuses the thread-scoped Context Detail Pane in an editor tab
- app-wide Usage remains the canonical aggregated platform view and is not replaced by this thread-scoped pane
- mid-stream updates are allowed but must use explicit in-progress states until final usage totals are known

The Context Detail Pane must support both curated inspection and raw payload inspection.

- curated overview of thread counts, provider/model/mode/persona, and headline tokens/context/estimated cost
- grouped context and token breakdowns
- per-message inspection with human-readable fields first
- raw payload toggles for the full thread and for individual messages
- drill-downs by mode, provider, model, and other shared runtime identity dimensions when available

- per-thread chat cost consumes canonical UsageRecord projections first
- OpenCode-style normalization is a display fallback only when the UsageRecord marks the value `pricing_estimated` or otherwise non-authoritative
- reasoning/thoughts, cache read, cache write, cache_write_1h/TTL, output_visible, provider_total, and context_estimate display only under the provider mapper's inclusive/exclusive `counting_semantics`
- provider-sensitive cache normalization caveats, source_class, source_confidence, settlement_status, freshness, and redaction state remain visible in raw/debug paths and must not be hidden behind authoritative wording in the chat UI

Canonical usage-source classes for Cursor are:
- `provider-reported`
- `team-admin-reported`
- `inferred_from_runtime_refusal`
- `inferred-from-runtime/editor-refusal`
- `/editor-refusal`

- PM must not invent a fake universal remaining-request counter when Cursor exposes only plan totals, team allotments, or runtime/editor refusal signals.
- Cursor browser-auth accounts may provide strong local per-run usage, but `/limit` and account-row truth require provider or team API augmentation; PM must not treat inferred per-run data as a `remaining-requests` source.
- Cursor headless/runtime evidence may include structured per-run token usage, account identity, version, active model, available models, MCP status, and session/request IDs; until official account-limit data is stronger, Cursor CLI pressure remains `/inferred` from runtime/API augmentation or editor/runtime refusal rather than a precise remaining balance.
- The `cursor` binary may be an editor/remote CLI surface, so Usage treats `cursor-agent` as the account/runtime evidence target when attributing `/remote` execution.
- Usage UI must disclose whether the data comes from provider-reported plan data, team-admin data, inferred-from-runtime evidence, or editor-refusal evidence.

Codex is a direct provider in PM and supports multiple accounts across two distinct auth families:
- `Sign in with ChatGPT`
- `Use API Key`

- ChatGPT-backed Codex usage and API-key-backed Codex usage are distinct entitlement buckets.
- PM MUST NOT merge those buckets into one shared pressure or cooldown pool, even when they belong to the same human owner.

- Usage rows must label the bucket plainly, for example `Plan: ChatGPT Pro` or `Usage Bucket: API billed`.
- The API-key path displays `Uses API-billed Codex access and separate API usage limits` when explaining a switch between API-key-backed Codex usage and ChatGPT-plan usage.
- Codex GUI labeling may use the template `Plan: ChatGPT <tier>` when the plan tier is known; `/chatgpt` denotes the browser/ChatGPT-plan-backed bucket rather than the API-key billing bucket.
- `codex login status` is an allowed local probe for direct Codex login state and reports whether the account is logged-in. PM records that as setup/status evidence, not as usage quantity or quota evidence.
- Codex ChatGPT `/browser` accounts may expose strong local `/runtime` stats, but provider/runtime rate-limit hints must be parsed separately from token statistics so a row does not confuse token usage with quota or rate-limit pressure.
- For API-key-backed Codex, `Use API Key` is the canonical setup path; optional import from existing key or auth material is future/secondary and is not required for the core usage model.

- if the user exhausts premium requests, Copilot can still fall back to included models for the rest of the month, but premium-request-backed behavior is subject to explicit block `/rate-limit/policy` state.
- premium-request exhaustion, paid-overage policy, org policy blocks, and entitlement-missing states are distinct conditions and must not all be flattened into a generic cooldown.
- blocked reasons should remain explicit, including `billing_entity_required`, `included_premium_exhausted`, `paid_overage_disallowed`, `copilot_entitlement_missing`, and `copilot_org_policy_blocked`.
- The default plain-language mapping for `included_premium_exhausted` is status `Premium requests exhausted`, subtext `Premium-request-backed features are unavailable until reset or policy change`, and secondary note `Included models may still be available` when included-model usage remains eligible.
- if multiple billing entities are available, the account may be `Logged in` but still `Needs setup` until the user chooses the effective billing entity.
- Usage and status surfaces must show the selected billing/entity context whenever it explains the active quota bucket.
- org/account metrics may strongly inform pressure, but exact hard-block semantics require explicit Copilot entitlement, policy, or runtime refusal evidence rather than inference from metrics alone.

- Team admin APIs such as `/metrics/spending` may inform Copilot pressure, but PM must not promise a simple per-account `remaining-requests` endpoint as account-row truth unless the provider exposes one.
- Team/enterprise request allotments, usage-based pricing controls, and admin `/dashboard/API` reporting are team-level augmentation surfaces; PM must keep `/enterprise` policy and billing context separate from per-account remaining-request truth.
- PM must not reduce Copilot pressure to only `has premium requests left` vs `does not`; provider evidence must preserve whether the account has premium requests left, does not, or is blocked by billing/entity, organization, or runtime-side entitlement policy.
- Paid overage disallowed by the selected organization `/enterprise` policy and provider `/runtime-side` auth or entitlement failures are distinct blocked/pressure causes.

- **Availability:** Anthropic **Admin API** (`/v1/organizations/usage_report/claude_code`); env: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Already documented in AGENTS.md.
- **What we get:** Organization-level usage and cost; `customer_type`, `subscription_type` for plan detection. Per-session usage also available from **stream-json** output when we use `--output-format stream-json` (usage events in the stream).
- **Usage feature:** Use Admin API for 5h/7d or org windows when key is set; use stream-json usage events for per-run tokens and optional mid-stream context %. No SDK required for CLI-based runs.
- API-backed Claude Code accounts can use authoritative cost and `/rate-limit` data to drive stronger `approaching_threshold`, `threshold_reached`, and `exhausted` pressure states.
- API-backed Claude Code accounts are the stronger path for precise cost `/token` reporting; subscriber-backed usage relies more on `/patterns`, runtime signals, and provider-reported limits that are not identical to API billing data.
- Claude Code subscriber-vs-API usage distinction is explicit: subscriber-backed Claude Code accounts, including Pro/Max style `/Max` sign-in, and API-backed or `/organization-backed` usage do not expose the same authoritative surfaces.
- Claude Code CLI subscription `/stats` visibility generally informs pressure; PM records `/exhaustion` only when the runtime or provider explicitly signals a hard block or exhausted state.
- API / Console / organization-backed Claude Code limits are org-level and may include monthly spend limits plus shorter-window rate limits such as `RPM` and `/TPM`; subscriber-backed rows must not reuse those hard limit semantics without provider evidence.
Gemini Direct usage must stay route-specific, and Antigravity CLI usage must be modeled as its own active CLI-runtime route where verified. Gemini CLI usage is retired/source-lineage only.
Usage must not revive Gemini CLI as a live provider row; active Google-owned CLI-runtime evidence belongs to Antigravity.
`Gemini` is the direct key-only, API-key-backed provider entry.

- direct Gemini account rows are API-key-backed only.
- quota identity may depend on effective Google project context as well as the key itself.
- Gemini direct API-key setup uses `GEMINI_API_KEY`; Vertex-family quota evidence may come through `ADC`, `gcloud`, service-account JSON, or a Google Cloud API key only when the selected provider entry and auth family support it.
- For direct Gemini setup, `Use API Key` is the canonical setup path; optional future import of existing key material is not required for the core model.
- when PM cannot prove authoritative remaining `/quota`, the UI must show `estimated`, `/unknown`, or equivalent source-qualified wording rather than pretending the numbers are definitive.
- Gemini API key paths are pay-as-you-go with tier/model-based rate limits instead of fixed Code Assist daily `/minute` counters.

| **AGENTS.md -- Usage Tracking & Plan Detection** | Canonical source for per-platform usage sources (Claude Admin API, Copilot metrics, Gemini quotas, Codex/Cursor error parsing), env vars, and error-message parsing. |
| **Plans/newfeatures.md §19.2** | Technical mechanism for 5h/7d (session usage from stream, account-level via `claude --account` or Admin API); mid-stream usage and context % from stream-json. |
